strategies.name: Sequential All-Reduce with Interleaved Scaling
strategies.desc: Uses 8 back-to-back all_reduce calls with element-wise scale/unscale operations between each stage, exactly as shown in the seed implementation. Requires 8 collective dispatches plus 14 local loops (7 scale operations, 7 unscale operations). Straightforward but potentially high latency due to sequential collective blocking.

strategies.name: Fused Scale-AllReduce with Precomputed Buffers
strategies.desc: Precomputes all scaling coefficient arrays once, then performs scale+all_reduce in tight loops to reduce intermediate clones and enable better kernel fusion. Still uses 8 all_reduce dispatches but reduces local operations by batching coefficient applications and eliminating redundant buffer allocations. Trades memory for fewer dispatch overheads.

strategies.name: Reduce-Scatter + All-Gather Pipeline
strategies.desc: Decomposes each all_reduce into reduce_scatter followed by all_gather, allowing pipeline overlap opportunities across the 8 stages. Uses 16 total collective dispatches (8 RS + 8 AG) but smaller per-rank payloads (S elements instead of W*S) during reduce_scatter phases. Exploits bandwidth-latency tradeoff at world_size=224.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level AllReduce Tree
strategies.desc: Exploits potential multi-node structure by performing intra-node all_reduce followed by inter-node all_reduce for each of the 8 stages. Uses 16 collective dispatches (8 stages × 2 levels) but with smaller payloads at the inter-node level. Benefits from lower latency on faster intra-node interconnects when num_nodes > 1.

strategies.name: Vectorized Shard-Parallel All-to-All Exchange
strategies.desc:
Reframes the problem as all-to-all personalized exchange where each rank computes its contribution to all shards, then uses all_to_all to redistribute. Requires 8 all_to_all collective dispatches instead of all_reduce. Payload size remains W*S but communication pattern may better utilize network bisection bandwidth on large-scale topologies.
